messages:
incident-bot: P1 alert - Pegasus enterprise (VPC) eu-west-1 dedicated pool showing elevated 500s and stream resets. Rule: dedicated_pool_conn_err_rate > 4% for 7m. Paging oncall-sre: alice. :rotating_light:

alice: Ack, I'm on it. Pulling health + logs for pegasus pools and peering lanes.

ben: Confirming TCP RSTs between edge-proxy-eu-west and pegasus-dedicated-eu-west. Multiple nodes reporting ENETUNREACH and connection churn. KV cache warmers failing.

alice: Seen on pool-02 and pool-03. Cache thrash + prefix misses, lots of retries. Looks like a networking peering flap or route blackhole.

carla: Pegasus CS says customers see streaming disconnects and stuck requests. They want an ETA and mitigation.

devon: Short term mitigation: shift traffic to the customer's standby warm capacity in eu-central-1. We'll do a staged weighted DNS cutover + edge-level retry/failover to avoid session storms.

alice: Proposed plan: 1) lower DNS TTL to 30s; 2) add weighted records: start 90% eu-west / 10% eu-central warm; 3) enable edge failover retry policy so backend errors route to warm; 4) serve lighter model on warm to reduce mem pressure; 5) monitor 15m and escalate to full cutover if error rate drops.

ben: Pushing edge failover (envoy) now. Will enable 2 retries and host-level failover to warm pool.

ben (code):
```
# envoy route retry snippet
routes:
  - match: /generate
    retry_policy:
      retry_on: 5xx,gateway-error
      num_retries: 2
      per_try_timeout: 2s
```

alice: Lowered Route53 TTL to 30s via CLI.

devon: Creating weighted DNS record to send 10% to eu-central warm VIP.

carla: Looping in the customer's SRE: @kevin. You'll see partial traffic on warm in ~1m. Please confirm session behavior.

kevin: Copy. I see a subset of sessions on the standby. Latency is higher but responses are succeeding.

eric: Deploying the 13b degraded model to warm and tagging responses with an x-model header for visibility. This will reduce memory pressure vs 70b variants.

alice: Canary (10%) active. Grafana dashboard: http://grafana/pegasus/pool-errors. Traces: http://traces/pegasus.

ben: Edge retry policy live. Early metrics: total error rate fell from 5.1% -> ~2.0%.

carla: Customer notified of partial shift; they want updates every 10m.

alice: Canary stable for 12m. Proceed to 30%.

ben: 30% live. Warm pool CPU/memory look healthy with the smaller model. Redis/kv hit rate improved.

devon: Added a circuit-breaker on heavy-model requests to warm to avoid memory spikes; heavy-model requests will be rejected to force fallback to eu-west if needed.

kevin: Customer reports majority of sessions recovered; a few legacy sessions still hitting eu-west and failing.

alice: Starting ramp: 50% -> 75% -> 100% over next 20 minutes, monitoring error rate <1% threshold.

ben: Ramp completed. At 100% new traffic is routing to eu-central warm VIP; eu-west nodes are in drain state.

carla: Created incident ticket INC-20260211-pegasus-warm-failover assigned to eng-networking and eng-runtime for RCA.

alice: Post-shift checklist: keep TTL low for 1h, keep warm pool scaled +25% buffer for 90m, collect heap/oom dumps from eu-west nodes, gather network traces and peering configs.

incident-bot: Note: on-call handoff to night-sre jordan scheduled in 40m. Current owner alice.

jordan: Ack, taking over watch. Will escalate on error rate >1% for 5m or median latency >1800ms. :eyes:

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (traffic on warm standby). RCA tasks remain open.

carla: I'll coordinate customer RCA meeting and timeline. Thanks team. :handshake:

kevin: Thanks all for the quick mitigation. The degraded model option was helpful to restore availability.

alice: I'll collect logs and follow up with eng-runtime and networking for root cause. Leaving edge failover enabled for 2h and scaling buffers in place.

ben: Will remove retry policy after stability window.

carla: Closing out real-time ops here. Keeping ticket open for RCA and forensics.
